title: Plymouth High’s Mascots Are the Panthers… and the Eagles?

content: Illustration by Dale Stephanos Welcome to “ The Salty Cod ,” a monthly column in which humorist Steve Calechman grapples with uniquely New England dilemmas. The only plausible explanation for passing on the perfect name is that the leaders of Plymouth had an even more perfect name. Except that they didn’t. It’s the Blue Eagles. It’s a classic American color for a classic American symbol, which no one would complain about, and yet no one would call inspired. It’s rare that a town gets a do-over. But when Plymouth South opened in 1989, it got to pick its own identity. Pilgrims was still available. And it chose…the Panthers. Whiff number 2. You have to admire the commitment. Other Massachusetts schools understand the assignment: the Charlestown Townies, Lexington Minutemen, Quincy Presidents, Lenox Millionaires. You hear those names and know exactly where you are. Eagles? No clue. And yet, in Massachusetts of all places, not one high school has claimed the Pilgrims or Puritans. Now, in fairness to Plymouth North and South, their yearbooks are the Pilgrim and the Rock , respectively, so it’s not like they’ve totally skipped history class, but with such good options sitting right there, why so many vanilla names? “They can’t offend anyone,” says Susan Westcott Alessandri, associate professor of advertising at Suffolk University. “I think it’s as simple as that.” And Plymouth is hardly alone. Sure, not every Massachusetts town has a Minuteman or Millionaire to work with. But you know what else most of them don’t have? Eagles, lions, or panthers. Panthers, in fact, are solitary creatures—another strike against them as a team mascot. Plymouth, you can try again. We believe in you. You want an animal? No problem. There are plenty that once roamed the state and haven’t been taken. The Gray Wolves. That’s both catchy and a touch literary. The Bison. Majestic and not-to-be-messed-with. But the winner might be the Elks. Great graphic design potential. Punchy sound. Easy to fit on a jersey. And just think of the deal they’d get at the local lodge for the annual banquet.
